chapter_theme: The one letter within the five: Namasivaya stands inside the body, the five senses are to be gathered into a single letter and silenced so that the Lord speaks, and the gates of the body open upward to a light beyond the sky. Around this Sivavakkiyar sets the one source that became castes and beings, the deniers who say 'it is not', those who do not bow, and, three times, the name of Rama; the breath known and let go keeps one a child.
structure_note: Letter-verses and the five letters (1064 to 1069, 1073) alternate with the images of becoming by thought (1070), the gates (1074, 1086) and the one that became many (1075, 1077). Rama's name enters at 1071 and returns at 1081 and 1082. 1079 and 1084 are in cipher; 1087 is the one breath instruction; 1088 closes with the lightning image shared with 1057 and with Pattirakiriyar.

1064.reading: Three and three and three, which the three gods seek; the three and the five letters, roaring within the letter A; the mother who bore, the father, and the moving nada: within the mandala that appears there is nowhere else to speak.
1064.nuance: The three threes are not keyed; tradition offers the three letters of Om, the three channels, the three regions. The verse reworks 1063 line by line, replacing the one letter with the mandala in which it sounds.

1065.reading: Lying curled like a dog, like a feeding ghost, fools who rose delighting in the stinking pit; if you can cut the snarl of the five who rage, you will become one in six among the six crore matted-haired ones.
1065.nuance: சீறுகின்ற ஐவர், the five that rage, are the senses; கும்பி, the pit, is the womb or the belly. சோறுகின்ற பூதம் is unclear (a being that feeds, or an element). The last line's six crore and 'one in six' has no key; perhaps the six adharas, perhaps the ranks of sages.

1066.reading: The space that deluded you within as a circle; within the eight-fold figure, the containing and the subsiding; within the moving wheel that is eight and eight and eight, what can be reached rose, once we had known our Lord.
1066.nuance: அட்டவக்கரம் may be the eight-letter mantra or an eight-cornered figure; எட்டும் எட்டும் எட்டும் (twenty-four) may count tattvas or petals. எட்டலாம் puns on எட்டு, eight, and எட்டல், reaching. The plain sense is that the body's wheel becomes legible after knowing the Lord, not before.

1067.reading: The one who speaks too is the Lord, and Brahma-knowledge is within you; the five who are desire wander and dispense grace; if you contain those five of desire into one letter and stay without speaking, the Lord will come and speak.
1067.nuance: அலைந்தருள் செய்கிறார் reads oddly, the senses 'graciously' wandering; it may be ironic, or அருள் may be corrupt. The exchange is the point: when the speaker falls silent, the Lord takes over the speaking. 1104 ends the same way.

1068.reading: The five letters Namasivaya and the higher states they give; in Namasivaya's five, the five, and the ancient maya; the five letters Namasivaya stand within us; Lord, speak well the truth of Namasivaya!
1068.nuance: அஞ்சில் அஞ்சும், the five within the five, is left open: the five elements, the five acts or the five senses. The verse puts maya too inside the five letters, so the mantra holds the binding as well as the release.

1069.reading: Supreme, there is no separate fear for you and for me; standing with hand raised and folding the hands in worship are what I owe; Lord of glory whose head melted and gave nectar: the strength you gave me is Om Namasivaya.
1069.nuance: பயம் may be fear or fruit, so line 1 may say there is no separate fruit for you and me. சிரம் உருகி அமுதளித்த, the head melting and giving nectar, is read in tradition as the yogic nectar from the crown; it may also be the moon on Siva's head. The verse accepts outward worship, unusually for this poet.

1070.reading: In its nest of fresh clay the hunter-wasp has set a browned worm; thinking daily, it becomes what it thought; the fresh clay breaks and it becomes the dragonfly that flies away; madmen, understand the shape the Lord fashions.
1070.nuance: The image rests on the belief that a worm sealed in the potter wasp's clay nest becomes a wasp by brooding on it; வேட்டுவன், hunter, is the wasp that hunts worms. One becomes what one holds in thought. A second reading has the clay as the body that breaks and the winged thing as the soul; பிச்சர்காள் may address the mad or the Lord's madmen.

1071.reading: For all who come and stay on luminous Kasi, Visvanatha, whose body is the open light, with the clear Lady beside him speaks the saving taraka: the easy name, Rama Rama, Rama the nectar.
1071.nuance: The tradition is that Siva at Kasi speaks the taraka mantra into the ear of the dying; Sivavakkiyar names it as Rama. A Saiva poet giving Siva the Rama name is the point, taken up in 1081 and 1082 and in 1095's refusal of two gods.

1072.reading: The yoni of the creeper grown from the eye and the water: one may babble of it in the open, but no fruit came of that; the land spread as space and the root knowledge within space: the strong jnanis who are clear stay clear, for certain.
1072.nuance: வில்லவல்லி யோனி is cipher; the creeper is Shakti and the yoni her source-figure, and the phrase returns in 1084. The verse contrasts speaking of it openly, which bears nothing, with the knowledge held within space. மூலவித்தை is the root knowledge or the root mantra.

1073.reading: Om Namasivaya: once one realises it and realises truth; once one realises it and truth clears; once one realises it and realises truth, Om Namasivaya stands mingled within.
1073.nuance: Three nearly identical lines and a fourth that lands: the verse is the chant it describes, and its only addition is the sequence realise, clear, realise, mingle. Nothing is said beyond the refrain.

1074.reading: The nine gates of trouble and the gate that reached meaning; the five gates that speak and what stood swelling and sobbing; opening the good gate and going through the gate of knowledge, those who have seen the boundary gate are not born again.
1074.nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings and the five the senses; the good gate (நல்ல வாசல்) is tradition's tenth gate at the crown. அருத்தடைந்த வாசல் and சொம்மிவிம்மி are unclear. 1086 opens the same upper gate.

1075.reading: The one that was first became forms upon forms, rose as the differences of caste and became every living being; after staying with the origin and rising again into birth, he becomes the jnani of light and stays pure.
1075.nuance: Caste (சாதிபேதம்) is listed among the forms the one took, so it is neither denied nor honoured here; 1098 and 1100 attack it. Line 3 is hard: who stays with the origin and is born again, the one or the soul, and whether the jnani is the one returned.

1076.reading: That the world blossomed with the blossoming pollen as its root; that the blossomed flower came with its intoxication, fed and let go; that the five senses with their organs were confused and fell on the earth; this dazzling, confused maya: what maya is this, Lord?
1076.nuance: The flower and its pollen are the figure for generation: the body grows from seed as the world from pollen, and ends with the senses fallen. The closing cry is 1043's.

1077.reading: All that is on the earth and all in the wide sky, the bright flame that stands joined to them without any place of its own; without anyone's place, within and without, the one who has seen its fine places knows Siva and is the jnani.
1077.nuance: ஓரிடமும் இன்றியே (without any one place) and சீரிடங்கள் கண்டவன் (who has seen its fine places) pull against each other on purpose: the light has no place, and the knower sees where it is.

1078.reading: Carrying clay vessels you climb the mountain and wander about; you say that things past counting are possible; how can one live together with men who do not bow daily to the Lord with their heads to the ground?
1078.nuance: மண்கிடாரம், the clay vessel, may be the body carried up the hill of life, or the pots carried to hill shrines; the boast of line 2 is of powers. The verse demands daily prostration, which sits oddly beside 1093 and 1094 unless the Lord bowed to is within.

1079.reading: That the book on the tongue perished, that goodness and caste perished, that the chariot one mounts perished, that inquiry lessened: sinners, what maya is this? When the left land becomes a quarrel, on the day the breath subsides the five subside too.
1079.nuance: The list of losses, learning, caste, vehicle, inquiry, reads as the ruin at death or as what falls away in realisation. வாமநாடு is obscure (the left region, perhaps the moon channel). ஐவரும் are the senses or the elements that subside with the life.

1080.reading: Poor ones who keep saying 'it is not, it is not': can what stands as 'not' be said not to be? It is neither 'not' nor a thing; those who have found the limit of what stands with the two joined are not born again.
1080.nuance: The target is the denier (perhaps the materialist, perhaps the Buddhist 'void'); the answer is a double negation, not nothing and not a thing, with the two joined. The verse circles what later Siddhars call சூனியம் without using the word.

1081.reading: Kara kara kara kara, guardian of the guarding aeon; pora pora pora pora, the meritorious one who stood in battle; mara mara mara mara, the one who shot the seven trees: the name that says Rama, Rama, Rama.
1081.nuance: The syllables are chosen so that மர reversed gives ராம, as in the story of the hunter who chanted 'mara' until it became 'Rama'; the seven trees are the sal trees Rama's arrow pierced. The verse is sound before it is sense, a mantra built from repetition.

1082.reading: Born on the wide earth with a body that is a mere interval: when release is said to be this, does one still need to want pleasure? Did the four Vedas, sung, spread over the earth? Seek the name that says Rama, Rama, Rama.
1082.nuance: நேரமான காயம், a body of a moment, or a body made to measure. Line 3 asks whether the Vedas spread over the earth, which may be a taunt (they did not) or a concession (they did, yet the name suffices). The name is set above both pleasure and scripture.

1083.reading: The life comes and takes a body by its goodness and stays; when the life leaves the body it becomes form upon form; the life becomes Siva's maya and they kill one another; the life becomes Shakti's maya and they eat one another.
1083.nuance: The mutual killing and eating of life and maya is the puzzle: tradition reads the soul lost in maya and maya dissolved by the soul's knowledge in turn. நன்மையால் may be by merit (the fruit of good deeds) or by the goodness of the Lord.

1084.reading: The long letter, the circle, and the full creeper's yoni; the long letter and one circle, I did not see one that stood; if, marking it with horn and foot, one says it is in the short letter, our Lord does not stand straight in the one circle of the long letter.
1084.nuance: A riddle in the terms of Tamil writing: நெட்டெழுத்து the long vowel, குற்றெழுத்து the short, கொம்பு and கால் the vowel signs (ெ and ா), வட்டம் the circle, which may be the letter ம, the zero or the bindu. Tradition reads the circle as the bindu and the creeper's yoni as Shakti's triangle; the plain point is that the Lord cannot be written down.

1085.reading: The true thing the gods in heaven cannot know, our Lord who stood mingled as the pupil within the eye; after cutting off birth on earth and setting his flower feet, the great one dwells within us: that is the truth.
1085.nuance: கண்ணில் ஆணி, the nail or pin in the eye, is the pupil: the Lord as what sees in the seer, taken up from 1042. The feet are set (மலரடிகள் வைத்தபின்) as the guru sets the feet on the disciple's head, and then the Lord is within.

1086.reading: Opening the upper gate of the light that stands beyond the sky, when it has entered and mingled within so that the eyes rejoice, forgetting the maya born of earth and its confusion, to stay in accord with the Lord mingled in thought is the truth.
1086.nuance: மேலைவாசல், the upper gate, is tradition's tenth gate at the crown, 1074's good gate. The light is beyond the sky yet enters within; the verse holds the two directions together.

1087.reading: Once you have known the breath within the root breath and let it go, if day after day you fix it as a single gaze before you, you can stay long as a child and become Parabrahman; by the oath of the poison-throated one and the oath of the Mother, this is true.
1087.nuance: The verse is the chapter's one plain instruction: know the breath, release it, hold it in attention daily. The promise is youth and the Supreme, sworn on Siva and Shakti. The word is மூச்சு, not the Siddhars' வாசி.

1088.reading: As lightning rises, lightning spreads and lightning subsides, the Lord within me who stands within me subsides within me; since the eye that stands in the eye does not know the straightness of the eye, I have known nothing but the one who stands within me.
1088.nuance: Two images for one claim: the lightning that rises and subsides in itself, and the eye that cannot see itself. The last line is the poet's confession that he knows only the one within, not the Lord as an object. Pattirakiriyar's Meynjanap Pulambal 177 (seq 180) has the same lightning line as a question, 'when shall I know?'.

links.note: 1064 reworks 1063 line by line: the letter in the three mandalas becomes three threes the gods seek, the mantra of mother and father gains the moving nada, and the one letter in which there is nowhere else to speak becomes the mandala in which it appears.

Both end with the Lord coming to speak once the human speaker falls silent or recites the one letter: 1067 contains the five senses in one letter and keeps silent; 1104 dismisses a hundred crore Agamas and recites the single rising letter.

Tirumular's five senses draw in like a tortoise when the silent letter meets the spoken one, and reaching Om gain inner light; Sivavakkiyar's five of desire are contained in one letter and silence, and the Lord speaks. In both the gathering of the senses follows the letter rather than effort.

Two creatures that become by thought: the turtle whose eggs hatch on the shore by her brooding from the sea (1062) and the worm in the wasp's clay nest that becomes a wasp by brooding (1070). 1062 applies it to contemplating the light within; 1070 to becoming what one thinks.

Tirumular's two breaths set in the upper palate open the door and end death; Sivavakkiyar's good gate opened and passed leads to the boundary gate and no more birth. Both set the body's upper opening against the nine ordinary ones.

The Kural says birth is alike for all beings and distinction comes from deeds; Sivavakkiyar says the one origin became the differences of caste and every being. Both deny that caste is primordial, the Kural by pointing to work and Sivavakkiyar to the one source.
The two verses share the cry என்னமாயம் ஈசனே: 1043 on the body thrown out at death, 1076 on the body's growth from pollen and the senses' fall. Birth and death are framed as one maya.

1078 asks how one can live with men who do not bow daily to the Lord; 1093 laughs at those who do rites to stone and asks whether gods can be stone. Read together, the daily bowing 1078 demands is to the Lord who stands as guard within (1093), not to the image.

Tirumular's Siddhanta formula is 'neither one nor two nor nothing, yet one'; Sivavakkiyar's answer to the deniers is 'neither not nor a thing, the two joined'. Both refuse the void and refuse plain duality in the same breath.

1054 asks whether body took life or life took body, and answers that the life does not die; 1083 takes the life beyond the body into its dealings with maya, where life and maya kill and eat one another, so that the survival 1054 asserts is not yet release.
The pupil in the eye: in 1042 the gods see by it while claiming 'mine' and 'yours'; in 1085 the Lord stands as the pin in the eye, the truth the gods cannot know, and dwells within once birth is cut.
1074's good gate and gate of knowledge, passed through to the boundary gate, is 1086's upper gate opened to the light beyond the sky. Both end in no more birth or no more maya.

Both promise childhood through breath: Tirumular's yogi with the breaths set in the palate sees grey hair and wrinkles change and becomes a child; Sivavakkiyar's knower of the root breath can stay a child long and become the Supreme.

Pattirakiriyar's pulambal asks when he will know, within himself, the one who stands within him, with lightning that rises and subsides into the sky; Sivavakkiyar states it: the Lord within subsides within and is all he has known. The same couplet, a plea in one and a claim in the other.
1071 has Siva at Kasi teaching the name of Rama; 1095 asks whether there can be two gods, ours and yours. The Rama verses put the second claim into practice.

source_issues: 1067: அலைந்தருள் செய்கிறார் reads oddly of the senses and may be corrupt.
1079: வாமநாடு is obscure and may be a corrupt place-name or technical term.
1082: ராமமென்னுன் appears to run two words together (ராமம் என்னும்).
1088 is paralleled almost word for word by Pattirakiriyar's Meynjanap Pulambal 177 (seq 180), as the corpus notes; one of the two poets has the line from the other or from a common stock.
